newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai SEC says investigate FinOne for inside trade.
newsitem.headline: Thai SEC says investigate FinOne for inside trade.

text.p: Thailand's Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is investigating the transactions involving Finance One officials to see if they have violated insider trading regulations, a senior SEC official said on Friday.

"We have to look at the transactions involving company executives to see if they violate Article 241 which relates to insider trading," Prasarn Trairatvorakul, deputy secretary-general of the SEC, told Reuters.

Prasarn said the firm's executives had sold a substantial amount of the company's shares since last year. They declared the transactions according to SEC's regulations and no one was accused of wrongdoing.
However, Prasarn said the SEC was obliged to carry out the investigation because these transactions happened before Finance One announced its plans to merge with Thai Danu Bank Plc .

"It is a normal procedure for the SEC. If a listed company's executives trade a large amount of shares, we have to monitor whether there is any major news or development following the transaction," he said. "And if that is the case, we have to investigate if there is insider trading involved."
"I can't say anything more about the probe. But I would like to stress that this is just an investigation and no one has been accused of anything," he added.
Finance One, Thailand's biggest finance company, was badly battered by liquidity problems and poor-quality assets caused by its heavy exposure to the depressed property sector.
The company is scheduled to formally announce the details of the merger later on Friday.
